evals.prompt: Design a hero section for a premium charity that works on ocean cleanup.
evals.expected_output: One batched intake message, then exactly 2 structurally different hero plans with full detail, then a self-critique with scores, then an approval gate with no code.
assertions: Asks all intake questions in a single message before producing any design
Contains exactly 2 options labelled A and B
Both options include theme, desktop ASCII layout, mobile re-composition, tokens block, signature element, animations, and event-based interactions
The two options differ in layout logic and palette logic, not just colour
Each option declares exactly three decorative colour roles
Each option's signature element is nameable in one noun-first sentence and passes the four-part test
Neither option uses cream + serif + terracotta, near-black + acid accent, gradient blobs, or a giant-stat hero without a charity-specific reason
Does not use 01/02/03 markers on non-sequential content
Includes a self-critique table with a 1-5 score per criterion and a weighted total
The self-critique records at least one concrete change per option
States whether live research was performed and cites no URL it did not open
Ends with an instruction to reply 'execute' and contains no implementation code

evals.prompt: Design a landing page for an artisanal sourdough bakery in Lisbon.
evals.expected_output: Full process. The AI-default trap here is cream + serif + terracotta.
assertions: Avoids cream + serif + terracotta unless the brief specifically requested it
Names at least one concrete real-world source that drives the palette and type choices
Each option's tokens block declares exactly three decorative colour roles with hex values
Each option's signature element passes the four-part test
Self-critique explicitly addresses whether the option resembles the cream+serif+terracotta default
No fabricated reviews or biographies are invented
Ends at the approval gate with no implementation code

evals.prompt: Give me 2-3 wireframe options for a SaaS dashboard hero.
evals.expected_output: Batched intake resolving ambiguity, 2 options delivered.
assertions: Recognizes the ambiguity of 'dashboard hero' and resolves or asks about it in the intake
Asks for aesthetic direction rather than defaulting to a dark-mode SaaS look
Delivers exactly 2 options and briefly notes it can provide a third on request
Each option declares exactly three decorative colour roles
Each option's signature element passes the four-part test
Neither option defaults to near-black + acid accent or a uniform icon-title-paragraph grid without justification
Includes a self-critique with scores and a weighted total per option
Stops at the approval gate and writes no implementation code

evals.prompt: Build the design from option B of eval 1. Follow the plan exactly.
evals.expected_output: Builds the page, then runs Step 7 verification including signature survival.
assertions: The build output is React + Tailwind (or the project's existing stack)
The signature element from the plan appears in the built output
Step 7a signature verification is reported: does the signature survive, yes or no
Step 7b copy verification is reported: any spelling or proper-noun issues
Step 7c colour budget verification is reported: how many decorative colours shipped
Step 7d quality floor is reported with each item pass/warn/fail
No raw hex values in component code — uses tokens
Honestly reports if anything failed rather than claiming success

evals.prompt: Fix this API 500 error. Here's the stack trace.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT activate. Negative test.
assertions: The skill does not activate on this prompt
If the skill activates anyway, its output declines the task and explains it only handles page design

evals.prompt: This landing page feels AI-generated — make it better. Here's the HTML.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT activate — belongs to page-enhancer. Negative test.
assertions: The skill recognizes that this is an enhancement task, not a new design
The skill either hands off to page-enhancer or explicitly states it only handles new designs
If the skill activates anyway, it asks whether the user wants a new design or an enhancement
